title: Minimal finite free resolutions over a Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and let $d\ge0$ be an integer. If $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le d$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], i.e. an exact sequence $0\to P_d\to\dots\to P_0\to M\to0$ with every $P_i$ projective, then there is an exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of $R$-modules $$0\to F_d\xrightarrow{\varphi_d}F_{d-1}\xrightarrow{\varphi_{d-1}}\cdots\xrightarrow{\varphi_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$$ in which every $F_i$ is a finite free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] ($F_i\cong R^{\oplus n_i}$ for an integer $n_i\ge0$) and $\varphi_i(F_i)\subseteq\mathfrak mF_{i-1}$ for $1\le i\le d$ (equivalently: every matrix coefficient of every $\varphi_i$ lies in $\mathfrak m$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CXF (lemma-what-kind-of-resolutions-Noetherian-local, line 26702), condition (7): a finite free resolution of length d, with its proof (Lemmas 00LP resolution-by-finite-free, 00O5 independent-resolution, 00NX finite-projective: finite projective over local is free); together with Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex, line 24608) used as in the proofs of Lemmas 00OA and 00OB (lines 26990--26994 and 27082--27086: 'we may assume all the maps in the complex F have the property that Im(F_i -> F_{i-1}) is contained in m F_{i-1}, because removing a trivial summand from the resolution can at worst shorten the resolution'). Tags verified in tags/tags: 0CXF,algebra-lemma-what-kind-of-resolutions-Noetherian-local; 00MT,algebra-lemma-add-trivial-complex

proof.text: If $d=0$, the assumed exact projective resolution identifies $M$ with the projective module $P_0$. Thus $M$ is finite projective because it is finitely generated, and it is finite free over the local ring: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, where a localization at an element outside $\mathfrak m$ is the original module because that element is a unit. This gives the required one-term finite free resolution, with no differential to minimize.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CXF (lemma-what-kind-of-resolutions-Noetherian-local), proof and its use of Lemmas 00O5 and 00NX, lines 26702--26720

proof.text: Assume $d\ge1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian], choose an exact resolution $\cdots\to F_2\to F_1\to F_0\to M\to0$ with every $F_i$ finite free. Let $K=\ker(F_{d-1}\to F_{d-2})$, with $K=\ker(F_0\to M)$ when $d=1$. The given projective resolution of length at most $d$ and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-kernel-projective] imply that this $K$ is projective. Since $K$ is a submodule of the finite free module $F_{d-1}$, it is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Therefore $K$ is finite projective.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] to the finite projective module $K$ at $\mathfrak m$. The resulting element outside $\mathfrak m$ is a unit in the local ring, so $K$ itself is finite free. Substituting this copy of $K$ for the leftmost term gives an exact finite free resolution $0\to F_d\to F_{d-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to0$ of length at most $d$, where $F_d=K$ and the first map is the inclusion into $F_{d-1}$.

Starting from this bounded finite free resolution, if some differential $\varphi_i:F_i\to F_{i-1}$ for $1\le i\le d$ has a matrix coefficient that is a unit, apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-unit-entry-splits]. After changing bases, the underlying complex is the direct sum of a smaller finite free complex and the identity complex $R\xrightarrow{1}R$ in degrees $i$ and $i-1$. The augmentation $F_0\to M$ vanishes on that identity summand: when $i=1$, its $R$ in degree $0$ is the image of $\varphi_1$ and $\varepsilon\varphi_1=0$; when $i>1$, the identity summand has no degree-$0$ term. Thus the augmentation factors through the smaller complex. Since the identity summand is exact, the smaller augmented complex stays exact.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex), statement and proof, lines 24608--24650; its application in the proof of Lemma Tag 00OA, lines 26989--26994

proof.text: Repeat the preceding cancellation while a unit coefficient occurs in any differential. Each cancellation decreases the sum of the finite ranks of the two affected terms, so the process terminates. In the terminal complex every matrix coefficient of every differential is a nonunit; in a local ring every nonunit belongs to $\mathfrak m$, hence $\varphi_i(F_i)\subseteq\mathfrak mF_{i-1}$ for all $1\le i\le d$. The resulting exact sequence is the required minimal finite free resolution.

split_report.blueprint: The five steps supply the local-algebra resolution used along the dependency chain of the final sentence of the proof of thm-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting: 'Every finite etale $Y_0$-scheme is the restriction of a finite etale $Y$-scheme'. Steps 1-3 establish a bounded finite free resolution; Steps 4-5 establish its minimality. These are not claims made directly in that blueprint sentence.

lean.statement: theorem exists_minimal_finite_free_resolution {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) [Module.Finite R M] (d : ℕ) (h : HasProjectiveResolutionLE M d) : ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution M, (∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (P.complex.X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite R (P.complex.X i) ∧ Module.Free R (P.complex.X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℕ, i < d → LinearMap.range (P.complex.d (i + 1) i).hom ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R (P.complex.X i)))
